The ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of Molecular Targets, version 2 (ESCAT v2): an evidence-based framework for ranking alterations as actionability and resistance biomarkers in precision oncology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Since the publication of the ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of Molecular Targets (ESCAT) in 2018, precision oncology has evolved substantially. Tumour-agnostic therapy approvals, expanding real-world evidence datasets, and the clinical recognition of genomic resistance biomarkers have created the need to revise the original framework. METHODS: The ESMO Precision Oncology and Taxonomy Committee convened an international expert panel to revise the ESCAT classification. Through iterative review of the evolving evidence-base, structured feedback rounds, and consensus discussions, the panel developed an updated actionability scale and a novel resistance scale. The revision followed three principles: explicit grading of uncertainty within actionable tiers, formal inclusion of tumour-agnostic eligibility criteria, and systematic classification of resistance biomarkers to complement sensitivity designations. RESULTS: ESCAT version 2 (ESCAT v2) introduces several substantive changes. Tier I is restructured into three categories, proven, inferred, and extrapolated, that carry the same clinical directive but differ in the level of certainty within the supporting evidence. The guideline introduces formal tumour-agnostic gating criteria, the ESMO Tumour-Agnostic Classifier and Screener (ETAC-S). Tier II is refined into three sub-tiers graded by prospective interventional evidence, high-quality real-world or non-prospective evidence, and replicated case-level evidence. Tier X is subdivided into alterations that are tested and found not to be predictive (X-A) and biomarker-therapy matches in which the therapy lacks meaningful activity in the biomarker-defined population (X-B). A parallel four-level resistance scale ranges from clinically validated resistance (contraindication) to preclinical or computational evidence (research use only). CONCLUSIONS: ESCAT v2 provides a comprehensive, evidence-graded framework for interpreting actionability and resistance biomarkers in cancer, enabling more nuanced communication among clinicians, patients, regulators, and researchers while preserving a clear directive to act when evidence supports patient benefit.

title: Nivolumab plus relatlimab with platinum-doublet chemotherapy versus nivolumab with platinum-doublet chemotherapy in stage IV or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer: clinical, translational, and patient-reported outcomes results from the phase II RELATIVITY-104 study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Programmed death 1-blocking antibody, nivolumab, plus lymphocyte-activation gene 3-blocking antibody, relatlimab, is approved for advanced melanoma. We report results from Part 2 of RELATIVITY-104, the first phase II, proof-of-concept, head-to-head study to evaluate first-line nivolumab plus relatlimab plus platinum doublet chemotherapy (PDCT) versus nivolumab plus PDCT in patients with stage IV/recurrent non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In Part 2, patients were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT or nivolumab plus PDCT. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and duration of response (DOR) per BICR, ORR and PFS by subgroups, and safety. Exploratory analyses included overall survival (OS), biomarker, translational, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: In part 2, the primary endpoint was not met (ORR, 51.3% for nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT versus 45.0% for nivolumab plus PDCT); PFS hazard ratio (HR; 90% confidence interval [CI]) was 0.89 (0.72 to 1.09). A trend towards improved clinical benefit was seen with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in a subgroup of patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) ≥1% and nonsquamous histology (ORR: 58.0% versus 39.6%; PFS: HR, 0.68; 90% CI 0.46 to 1.01). A potential improvement in OS was observed with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in the PD-L1 ≥1% nonsquamous subgroup (HR, 0.60; 90% CI 0.38 to 0.94). The safety profile of nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT was manageable and consistent with previous reports. CONCLUSION: In RELATIVITY-104, the addition of relatlimab to standard-of-care did not improve outcomes in the unselected all-randomized population. However, positive trends observed in the subgroup of patients with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% and nonsquamous NSCLC supports further investigation in these patients in the phase III RELATIVITY-1093 study. CLINICALTRIALS: gov identifier: NCT04623775.

title: Overall survival with adjuvant ribociclib plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in patients with high-risk HR+/HER2– early breast cancer: Six-year follow-up of the NATALEE trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ribociclib plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (NSAI) demonstrated a statistically significant invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) benefit over NSAI alone in patients with hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) early breast cancer (EBC) at the primary efficacy analysis of the phase 3 NATALEE trial. This prespecified 6-year analysis assessed overall survival (OS) and other efficacy outcomes as well as safety. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients were adults with HR+/HER2- EBC and anatomic stage IIA (N1 or N0 with high-risk factors), IIB, or III disease. Enrolled patients were randomized 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off for 3 years) plus NSAI (letrozole 2.5 mg/day or anastrozole 1 mg/day for 5 years) or NSAI alone. Premenopausal women and men also received goserelin. The primary endpoint was iDFS, and secondary/exploratory endpoints included OS, distant disease-free survival (DDFS), and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS). RESULTS: With a median OS follow-up of 66.5 months, ribociclib plus NSAI demonstrated an OS benefit over NSAI alone (6-year ΔOS, 2.1%; HR, 0.809 [95% CI: 0.661-0.989]; nominal 1-sided P = .019), which was generally consistent across key subgroups. An increasing iDFS benefit with ribociclib plus NSAI was also observed (6-year ΔiDFS, 5.3%; HR, 0.741 [95% CI: 0.646-0.849]; nominal 1-sided P < .0001), which was also generally consistent across key subgroups. DDFS (HR, 0.744 [95% CI: 0.646-0.858]) and DRFS (HR, 0.738 [95% CI: 0.634-0.858]) results supported these findings. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: This prespecified descriptive 6-year OS analysis demonstrated positive OS results with a clinically relevant benefit of ribociclib plus NSAI, consistent with the increasing reduction in recurrence risk. These results reinforce the benefit of ribociclib plus NSAI in the adjuvant setting across the broad NATALEE-eligible population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03701334 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO)
authors: S. Cathrien S. Tromp – van Driel
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

title: Perioperative pembrolizumab or placebo plus neoadjuvant cisplatin and gemcitabine in participants with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are eligible for cisplatin: the double-blind, phase III KEYNOTE-866 study
abstract: Background Perioperative PD-(L)1 inhibitors, either combined with cisplatin-based chemotherapy or enfortumab vedotin, have improved outcomes in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are cisplatin eligible. The double-blind, phase III KEYNOTE-866 study evaluated perioperative (neoadjuvant and adjuvant) pembrolizumab versus placebo added to neoadjuvant cisplatin plus gemcitabine (chemotherapy) and radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (cystectomy) in MIBC. Patients and methods Eligible participants were aged ≥18 years, had centrally assessed clinical stage T2-T4aN0M0 or T1-T4aN1M0 MIBC with ≥50% urothelial histology, and were eligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and cystectomy. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo plus chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, followed by cystectomy, and adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo every 3 weeks for 13 cycles (pembrolizumab or placebo group, respectively). Primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by investigator assessment. Pathological complete response (pCR) rate by blinded independent central pathological review and overall survival (OS) were key secondary end points. Safety was a secondary end point. Results Overall, 907 participants were randomly assigned (pembrolizumab, n = 453; placebo, n = 454). Median follow-up was 60.9 months (range, 40.7-78.7). At 60 months, the estimated EFS rate was 63.5% with pembrolizumab versus 61.9% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.71-1.10; one-sided P = 0.1366). The pCR rate was 44.4% versus 35.8% (estimated difference 8.9%; 95% CI 2.5-15.1); median OS was not reached in both groups (hazard ratio 1.00; 95% CI 0.79-1.27). Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 99.8% of participants in the pembrolizumab group (grade ≥3 in 80.2%) and 98.7% in the placebo group (grade ≥3 in 75.1%). Conclusions The addition of perioperative pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and cystectomy did not confer a statistically significant EFS benefit in participants with MIBC who are cisplatin eligible. The safety profile of pembrolizumab was manageable and consistent with prior reports.

title: Capivasertib plus abiraterone in PTEN-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: updated survival analysis from CAPItello-281
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) have poor prognosis and reduced benefit from current standard of care. The phase III CAPItello-281 study (NCT04493853) showed a statistically significant benefit in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) with capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (combined with prednisone/prednisolone and androgen deprivation therapy): hazard ratio (HR) 0.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.98; P = 0.034. The HR for interim overall survival (OS; 26% maturity) was 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15. Here, we report ad hoc, descriptive analyses at 42% OS data maturity. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with de novo mHSPC and PTEN-deficient tumors (defined as ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic staining by immunohistochemistry) received capivasertib plus abiraterone or matched placebo (randomly assigned 1 : 1) plus abiraterone. Analyses carried out at this ad hoc data cut-off, including the alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint of OS as well as the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed rPFS, were descriptive and not prespecified in the protocol. RESULTS: A total of 1012 patients received capivasertib plus abiraterone (n = 507) or placebo plus abiraterone (n = 505). At this ad hoc analysis at 42% OS maturity (data cut-off: 9 March 2026), with 17 months' additional follow-up (median follow-up 39 months in both arms), HR for OS favored capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99, P = 0.044) and OS medians were reached: 57.4 versus 46.5 months. Updated rPFS (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.99, nominal P = 0.033; median 35.5 versus 26.0 months) was consistent with the primary analysis. The safety profile remained consistent with the primary findings. CONCLUSIONS: With longer follow-up, findings from this updated descriptive analysis support the clinically meaningful OS benefit of adding capivasertib to abiraterone in the treatment of patients with PTEN-deficient mHSPC. Capivasertib plus abiraterone represents a first-in-class targeted treatment approach for this poor prognosis population with high unmet need.

title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus gemcitabine–cisplatin followed by postsurgical adjuvant nivolumab versus neoadjuvant gemcitabine–cisplatin in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer: final results from the phase III CA017-078 trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative immune-checkpoint inhibition improves outcomes in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). The phase III, randomized CA017-078 (ENERGIZE) trial evaluated perioperative nivolumab plus neoadjuvant gemcitabine-cisplatin (GC) versus neoadjuvant GC alone for previously untreated, resectable MIBC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Adults with previously untreated cT2-T4aN0M0 MIBC eligible for radical cystectomy (RC) and cisplatin were randomized to neoadjuvant nivolumab plus GC followed by RC and adjuvant nivolumab (nivolumab plus GC arm), or neoadjuvant GC followed by RC alone (GC arm). Co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response (pCR; defined as ypT0N0) and event-free survival (EFS). Overall survival (OS) was a secondary endpoint within the prespecified hierarchical testing strategy, and formal testing was contingent on a statistically significant EFS result. RESULTS: At this final analysis with 54.5 months of median follow-up, 325 patients were randomized to the nivolumab plus GC arm, 328 to the GC arm. pCR rates were 39.1% and 29.6%, respectively (adjusted difference 9.5%, 99.91% CI -2.6-21.6). EFS was not improved in the nivolumab plus GC versus GC arm (104 events in each arm; HR 0.94, 95.74% CI 0.71-1.25; P=0.6697). OS was summarized descriptively because EFS did not meet the testing criterion (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.64-1.21). Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 50.0% versus 49.5%; one treatment-related death occurred with nivolumab plus GC. Pretreatment ctDNA was positive in 229/416 tested patients (55%) overall, 108/211 (51%) in the GC arm, and 121/205 (59%) in the nivolumab plus GC arm. Clearance by cycle 4 day 1 (C4D1) occurred in 153/199 patients (76.9%) overall, 87/107 (81.3%) with nivolumab plus GC, and 66/92 (71.7%) with GC. ctDNA detection at baseline and at C4D1 was associated with shorter EFS and OS. CONCLUSIONS: The addition of perioperative nivolumab to neoadjuvant GC did not improve outcomes and was associated with predictable toxicity. Exploratory analysis showed ctDNA was strongly prognostic.

title: Atirmociclib and fulvestrant for patients with HR+/HER2– advanced/metastatic breast cancer who progressed on a prior cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitor: primary analysis of the randomized FourLight-1 trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atirmociclib is a potential first-in-class, highly selective cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4 inhibitor, demonstrating significantly greater selectivity over CDK6. In a phase 1/2a study, atirmociclib plus endocrine therapy was well tolerated and showed encouraging antitumor activity in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced/metastatic breast cancer (mBC). We present results from a randomized study of atirmociclib plus fulvestrant versus investigator's choice of therapy (ICT) in patients with HR+/HER2- mBC whose disease progressed on prior adjuvant or first-line CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment. PATIENTS AND METHODS: FourLight-1 is an open-label, phase 2 study. Patients were randomized 1:1 to atirmociclib (300 mg orally, twice daily, continuously) plus fulvestrant or ICT (fulvestrant alone or everolimus plus exemestane). The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), and safety. RESULTS: At the data cutoff (12 January 2026), 263 patients were enrolled (atirmociclib, n = 126; ICT, n = 137; median age: 57 years). PFS was significantly improved with atirmociclib versus ICT (stratified hazard ratio: 0.60; 95% CI, 0.440-0.825; 1-sided P = 0.0007; median: 9.4 vs 6.6 months). A consistent PFS benefit was observed across most subgroups. Patients with baseline measurable disease in the atirmociclib arm had a higher ORR versus the ICT arm (21 [19.3%] vs 13 [11.3%]; nominal 2-sided P = 0.0901) and median DOR was numerically longer (14.8 vs 9.3 months, respectively); CBR was 61.9% versus 46.0%, respectively. The most common any-grade treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in the atirmociclib arm were neutropenia (47.2%), leukopenia (33.6%), and diarrhea (28.0%); 6.4% of patients discontinued atirmociclib due to TEAEs. CONCLUSIONS: Atirmociclib plus fulvestrant showed significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement in patients who progressed on prior CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment with a manageable safety and tolerability profile.

title: Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy for HR+/HER2− PD-L1‒Positive Advanced Breast Cancer: Final Analysis of the Phase 3 KEYNOTE-B49 Study
abstract: Background We evaluated pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in participants with PD-L1‒positive, hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/HER2- advanced breast cancer after progression on prior endocrine-based therapy (ET). Patients and methods Participants with locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥1 who had prior ET and were candidates for first-line chemotherapy were randomized to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo Q3W plus chemotherapy. The primary and key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review and overall survival (OS), respectively, in participants with PD-L1 CPS ≥1. PFS and OS in participants with PD-L1 CPS ≥10 and safety were secondary endpoints. Following protocol amendment, the sample size was reduced due to low PD-L1 prevalence. Results 342 participants were randomized. At interim analysis (median follow-up, 29.1 months), the hazard ratio (HR) for PFS was 0.74 (95% CI, 0.58‒0.95; P=0.0089 [significance criterion met]) favoring pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy (median [95% CI] PFS, 6.7 [6.2‒8.3] versus 6.0 [4.2‒8.1] months). HR for PFS in participants with PD-L1 CPS ≥10 numerically favored pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy (0.59; 95% CI, 0.35‒0.98). At final analysis (median follow-up, 34.9 months), HR for OS was 1.04 (95% CI, 0.81‒1.33; P=0.6185) for pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy (median [95% CI] OS, 21.0 [18.9‒22.9] versus 22.2 [17.6‒26.3] months). Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 38% of participants in the pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy arm and 33% in the placebo plus chemotherapy arm; 11% and 5% discontinued treatment due to treatment-related AEs, respectively. Conclusion In participants with PD-L1‒positive (CPS ≥1) HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy demonstrated statistically significant improvement in PFS, with no new safety signals observed. A numerical effect favoring pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy for PFS was observed in participants with PD-L1 CPS ≥10. No significant OS improvement was observed. Clinical trial registration KEYNOTE-B49; ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04895358.

title: Adjuvant chemotherapy with cisplatin and gemcitabine compared to standard of care after curative intent resection of cholangiocarcinoma and muscle invasive gallbladder carcinoma (ACTICCA-1/AIO-HEP-0112 trial)
abstract: Background Despite curative resection and adjuvant capecitabine, about 50% of biliary tract cancer (BTC) patients have tumour recurrence or die within two years. Combination chemotherapy with cisplatin and gemcitabine (CisGem) is an established palliative chemotherapy regimen BTC, which has been evaluated in the adjuvant setting here. Patients and methods ACTICCA-1 is a randomized, phase III investigator-initiated trial. Patients were enrolled at 67 sites across 8 countries between September 2017 and January 2023 and randomized to CisGem or capecitabine as adjuvant treatment regimen, each for a planned duration of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint is disease-free survival (DFS). Secondary endpoints include overall survival, safety and tolerability. Results 591 patients have been randomized. Median follow-up was 4.8 years. Median age was 63, 46.9% were female, and median interval between surgery and enrolment was 67 days. Primary tumour location was intrahepatic in 28.3%, perihilar in 19%, distal in 36.5%, and gallbladder in 16.2%, 47.9% of patients had lymph node positive disease (N+). CisGem showed a median DFS of 25.7 months compared to 17.9 months for capecitabine (log rank p=0.097). As pre-defined in the statistical analysis plan (SAP), due to violation of proportional hazard assumption a Cox model was not feasible and restricted mean survival time (RMST) was analysed. Patients receiving CisGem experienced on average 2.6 additional DFS months (95% CI 0.6-4.68) compared to capecitabine (RMST in the first 3 years, p=0.011), but no significant improvement in overall survival (RMST p=0.076; median 58.1 vs. 48.2 months). Toxicity showed a higher number of Severe Adverse Events (SAE) (130 vs. 113 with 51 vs. 47 assessed as treatment related) and a higher AE rate of 74.7% vs. 69.5% with CisGem compared to capecitabine. Conclusion CisGem did not statistically improve DFS compared to capecitabine and should thus not be applied as standard of care in the adjuvant setting. Trial registration The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02104882) and the EudraCT Nr: 2012-005078-70 / EU-CT-Nr.: 2024-517340-61-00.

title: Overall survival from the phase III postMONARCH trial of abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant for HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer following progression on a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy
abstract: BACKGROUND: The phase III postMONARCH trial demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) with abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant in participants with HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer (ABC) after disease progression on prior CDK4/6i plus endocrine therapy (ET). Here we report the prespecified final overall survival (OS) analysis. PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients had disease progression on a CDK4/6i plus aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for ABC or recurrence on or after adjuvant CDK4/6i plus ET. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive abemaciclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus fulvestrant. The final OS analysis was pre-specified at 200 OS events (HR boundary 0.753). Time-to-event analyses used the Kaplan-Meier method, and stratified Cox models were used to estimate the HR and 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: A total of 368 participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to abemaciclib plus fulvestrant (n = 182) or placebo plus fulvestrant (n = 186). At data cutoff, median follow-up was approximately 37 months; 200 OS events were observed (90 [50%] vs 110 [59%]). Median OS was 32.1 months with abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus 24.6 months with placebo plus fulvestrant (HR, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60 to 1.06]; P = 0.11, boundary for significance not reached). OS differences were consistent across subgroups. Updated PFS was consistent with the primary analysis (HR, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.62 to 0.99]; nominal P = 0.039). Time to second progression and chemotherapy-free survival also favored abemaciclib plus fulvestrant. Safety was consistent with the established abemaciclib profile with no new signals identified. CONCLUSION: Abemaciclib plus fulvestrant resulted in numerically longer median OS versus placebo plus fulvestrant, though statistical significance was not reached. The totality of evidence supports consideration of abemaciclib-based treatment for patients with HR+, HER2- ABC after disease progression on prior CDK4/6i plus ET. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05169567.

title: A randomized Phase 1 study of telisotuzumab adizutecan (ABBV-400, Temab-A) in combination with bevacizumab versus trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer
abstract: BACKGROUND: Telisotuzumab adizutecan (ABBV-400, Temab-A) is an antibody-drug conjugate targeting c-Met (MET) protein with adizutecan, a novel topoisomerase 1 inhibitor payload. In monotherapy dose escalation, Temab-A demonstrated a manageable safety profile and promising antitumor activity in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC; NCT05029882). Based on these results, a randomized cohort of Temab-A + bevacizumab (Bev) versus trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) + Bev (standard-of-care) was added with the hypothesis that addition of Bev would enhance efficacy. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Days 1-5 and 8-12 Q4W + Bev 5.0 mg/kg Q2W. Primary objectives were safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of Temab-A + Bev. RESULTS: Overall, 83 patients received treatment with Temab-A + Bev (n=63) or FTD-TPI + Bev (n=20) with median 3 (range, 1-8) prior lines of treatment and median follow-up of 18.2 months. Treatment-related adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal and hematological with low discontinuation rates (Temab-A 2.0: 3/26 [12%]; Temab-A 2.4: 1/30 [3%]). Objective response rate was 19% and 30% with Temab-A 2.0 and 2.4 + Bev, respectively, and 0% with FTD-TPI + Bev. For Temab-A 2.0 and 2.4 + Bev vs FTD-TPI + Bev, median progression-free survival was 5.6 and 6.8 months vs 4.2 months; median overall survival was 11.2 (HR=0.75) and 14.7 months (HR=0.62) vs 10.2 months, respectively. CONCLUSION: Temab-A 2.4 mg/kg + Bev demonstrated the most favorable risk-benefit profile, was tolerable, and had clinically meaningful improvements in efficacy versus FTD-TPI + Bev for advanced CRC. The regimen is being evaluated in the global randomized Phase 3 trial AndroMETa-560 (NCT07525206).

title: Final results of nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab or chemotherapy in microsatellite instability-high/mismatch repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer from CheckMate 8HW
abstract: BACKGROUND: The phase III CheckMate 8HW trial met its dual primary endpoints of superior progression-free survival (PFS) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (NIVO + IPI) versus chemotherapy [first-line (1L)] and versus NIVO (all lines) in patients with centrally confirmed microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H)/mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). We report prespecified final overall survival (OS) analyses and updated efficacy outcomes. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Immunotherapy-naïve adults with mCRC across different lines and MSI-H/dMMR by local testing were randomly assigned 2 : 2 : 1 to NIVO (240 mg) plus IPI (1 mg/kg) once every 3 weeks for four doses and then NIVO 480 mg once every 4 weeks; NIVO (240 mg) once every 2 weeks (six doses) and then 480 mg once every 4 weeks; or chemotherapy ± targeted therapies. Secondary endpoints include PFS in NIVO + IPI versus NIVO (1L) and OS and objective response rate in the centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR population. RESULTS: In total, 839 patients across all lines were randomly assigned; efficacy analyses were conducted in those with centrally confirmed MSI-H/dMMR. Median follow-up across all lines and treatment groups was 68.0 months (range 37.6-81.4 months). NIVO + IPI demonstrated significant OS benefit compared with NIVO across all lines [hazard ratio (HR) 0.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.46-0.82, P = 0.0009] and with chemotherapy in 1L (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.24-0.57, P < 0.0001). Clinically meaningful OS benefit was noted with 1L NIVO + IPI versus NIVO (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44-0.99, P = 0.0432), not meeting the prespecified threshold for significance (P < 0.006). PFS continued to favor NIVO + IPI across all three comparisons: NIVO (all lines; HR 0.60), chemotherapy (1L; HR 0.21), and NIVO (1L; HR 0.68). Grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 78 (22%) versus 50 (14%) patients treated with NIVO + IPI versus NIVO across all lines, with no new safety concerns or additional treatment-related deaths from the previous follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: NIVO + IPI showed significant OS benefit compared with NIVO across all lines and with chemotherapy in 1L, while providing a clinical OS benefit versus NIVO in 1L, reinforcing its standard-of-care status in MSI-H/dMMR mCRC.

title: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib with belzutifan or quavonlimab as first-line therapy for advanced renal-cell carcinoma: randomized open-label phase 3 LITESPARK-012 study
abstract: Background Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is a first-line standard of care for advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The phase 3 LITESPARK-012 study (NCT04736706) evaluated efficacy and safety of adding belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor) or quavonlimab (anti-CTLA-4) to this regimen. Participants and methods Adults with previously untreated advanced ccRCC were randomized 1:1:1 to 400 mg pembrolizumab IV Q6W plus 20 mg lenvatinib orally daily and 120 mg belzutifan orally daily (Arm A); coformulated quavonlimab/pembrolizumab 25 mg/400 mg IV Q6W (collectively called MK-1308A) plus lenvatinib (Arm B); or standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib (Control). Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal from study; pembrolizumab or quavonlimab/pembrolizumab were administered for a maximum of ∼2 years. Progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review and overall survival (OS) were dual primary endpoints, tested in all randomized participants for Arm A versus Control, and in participants with IMDC intermediate/poor risk or all participants for Arm B versus Control. Safety was a secondary endpoint. Results Overall, 560 participants were randomized to Arm A, 562 to Arm B, and 566 to Control. As of the data cutoff date (February 4, 2026), median follow-up was 43.6 months (range, 31.8-57.4). Among all participants, median PFS was 20.8 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.08, 95%CI 0.93-1.26; P=0.8408), 20.7 months in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.07, 95%CI 0.92-1.25; nominal P=0.8174), and 23.7 months in the Control arm; median OS was 52.0 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.04, 95%CI 0.87-1.25; P=0.6622), not reached (NR) in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.35; nominal P=0.8955), and NR in the Control arm. Among participants with intermediate/poor risk, median PFS was 20.5 months in Arm B and 23.5 months in the Control arm (HR 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.33; P=0.8954); median OS was 39.1 versus 46.2 months (HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.96-1.42; P=0.9419). Any-grade all-cause adverse events led to any-drug discontinuation in 51.6%, 51.4%, and 36.2% of participants in the A, B, and Control arms. Conclusions Neither addition of the HIF-2α inhibitor belzutifan nor the CTLA-4 inhibitor quavonlimab to pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improved outcomes in participants with previously untreated advanced RCC versus pembrolizumab and lenvatinib alone. Higher drug discontinuation rates due to adverse events occurred in the investigational arms. Efficacy and safety of standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib was consistent with prior reports.

title: Final prespecified analysis of the phase 3 LITESPARK-011 study: belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib for advanced renal cell carcinoma after anti–PD-(L)1 therapy
abstract: BACKGROUND: The phase 3, randomized, open-label LITESPARK-011 trial (NCT04586231) investigated belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib in participants with advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (ccRCC) following anti-PD-(L)1 therapy. At earlier analyses, belzutifan plus lenvatinib significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) and objective response rate (ORR) versus cabozantinib. Overall survival (OS) was tested but did not reach significance. We present the final analysis of LITESPARK-011. PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Adult participants with advanced ccRCC that progressed on or after anti-PD-(L)1 therapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to 120 mg belzutifan plus 20 mg lenvatinib or 60 mg cabozantinib orally once daily until disease progression or unacceptable adverse events. Dual primary endpoints were PFS by blinded independent central review (BICR) and OS. ORR by BICR was a key secondary endpoint; safety and duration of response (DOR) by BICR were secondary endpoints. RESULTS: At final analysis, median time from randomization to data cutoff date (2 February 2026) was 38.8 months (range, 29.1-59.0). 371 participants were assigned to belzutifan plus lenvatinib and 376 to cabozantinib. Belzutifan plus lenvatinib continued to demonstrate benefit versus cabozantinib in PFS (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.62-0.88), ORR (53.1% vs 40.2%), and DOR (22.0 vs 11.9 months). Mature OS results did not reach statistical significance at final analysis (median 33.7 versus 28.6 months; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.70-1.03; one-sided P=0.04689 [prespecified boundary 0.0223]). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 85.4% of the belzutifan plus lenvatinib group versus 83.0% of the cabozantinib group. CONCLUSIONS: Belzutifan plus lenvatinib continued to demonstrate PFS, ORR, and DOR benefit versus cabozantinib with additional follow-up; OS favored the combination but did not reach statistical significance at final analysis. Safety profile of belzutifan plus lenvatinib remained consistent with each drug as monotherapy. These findings continue to support belzutifan plus lenvatinib as a treatment option in advanced ccRCC following anti-PD-(L)1 therapy.

title: Clinical Complete Response with Dostarlimab Monotherapy in dMMR/MSI-H Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: First Results from the Global AZUR-1 Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multimodal treatment with chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) is a standard of care (SOC) associated with significant toxicity/morbidity. After TNT, clinical complete response (cCR) ranges between 21-41%, highlighting the need for novel approaches. dMMR/MSI-H tumors are exceptionally responsive to PD-1 blockade: in a pilot study, patients with dMMR/MSI-H LARC achieved durable responses after neoadjuvant dostarlimab. AZUR-1 is the first global registrational study evaluating dostarlimab monotherapy in adults with previously untreated stage II/III dMMR/MSI-H LARC. METHODS: Dostarlimab 500 mg was administered intravenously Q3W for 9 cycles. Key endpoints include rate of sustained cCR for 12 months (cCR12) following end of treatment (EOT) with dostarlimab alone by investigator and independent central review (ICR), and composite rate of cCR12 (INV) + pathological CR (pCR). RESULTS: At data cutoff (April 20, 2026), 154 patients were enrolled (median follow-up [range]: 26.3 [2-36] months). Of 144 patients with ≥12 months follow-up, 68% achieved cCR12 (INV). pCR was achieved in 12/15 patients (80%) who underwent surgery after dostarlimab alone: cCR12+pCR rate was 76%. cCR12 (ICR) was less mature than investigator, as first cCR (ICR) was identified at later timepoints. 98% who achieved cCR maintained cCR for ≥12 months. Overall, 93% of patients were on study with no evidence of disease progression after treatment (dostarlimab ± SOC); 71% achieved this outcome with dostarlimab alone. There were no reported recurrences for patients in cCR or pCR. Safety was acceptable; grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs occurred in 4 (3%) patients. PROs showed meaningful improvements from baseline to EOT for several domains. CONCLUSIONS: In this AZUR-1 interim analysis, 68% of patients achieved cCR12 and 76% achieved cCR12+pCR with dostarlimab alone and had no disease recurrences. These durable responses indicate the potential to eliminate the need for current SOC and redefine the curative-intent treatment paradigm with dostarlimab in dMMR/MSI-H LARC. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05723562.

title: A randomised phase III trial of adjuvant treatment intensification with mFOLFIRINOX versus mFOLFOX6 in high-risk stage III colon cancer: Results of the international IROCAS study.
abstract: Background Patients with pT4 and/or pN2 stage III colon cancer remain at high risk of recurrence despite oxaliplatin-based adjuvant chemotherapy. We evaluated whether intensification with modified FOLFIRINOX improved outcomes compared with modified FOLFOX6. Patients and methods In this international, academic, open-label, randomised phase III trial conducted by PRODIGE in France, CCTG in Canada, and GONO in Italy, patients with stage III colon adenocarcinoma after R0 resection presenting T4 and/or N2 were randomly assigned (1:1) to mFOLFIRINOX or mFOLFOX6 every 2 weeks for 12 cycles. The primary endpoint was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS) in the intention-to-treat population. Results Between May 2017 and June 2023, 795 patients were assigned to mFOLFIRINOX (n=398) or mFOLFOX6 (n=397). Median age was 59 years (range 19-75); 39.7% were women, 52.8% had pT4 disease, 72.2% had pN2 disease, and 25.3% had both. At a median follow-up of 55 months (IQR 42.6-65.9), 284 DFS events had occurred: 146 with mFOLFIRINOX and 138 with mFOLFOX6. Three-year DFS was 65.6% versus 66.3%, respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 1.07, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84-1.36; P=0.61). Although Overall survival (OS) data remain immature, 3-year OS was 91.2% versus 86.7% (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.61-1.21; P=0.37); no significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction was observed. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 62.2% and 62.1% of patients, respectively. Grade ≥3 diarrhoea (15.6% versus 3.8%) and fatigue (7.3% versus 1.8%) were more frequent with mFOLFIRINOX, whereas grade ≥3 neutropenia was less frequent (18.0% versus 23.9%). G-CSF use was 37.8% versus 19.1%. Conclusion Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX triplet chemotherapy did not improve DFS compared with standard doublet mFOLFOX6 in patients with high-risk stage III colon cancer. These findings do not support empirical chemotherapy intensification and highlight the need for novel adjuvant strategies. Clinicaltrials Gov identifier NCT02967289.

title: Pembrolizumab with or without platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line treatment in advanced NSCLC expressing PD-L1 ≥50%: The PERSEE randomized phase III trial (GFPC 01-2020)
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab, alone or combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, is a standard first-line treatment for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable oncogenic alterations and with high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of these two treatment strategies. METHODS: In this multicenter, phase III trial (PERSEE, NCT04547504), adult patients with treatment-naïve stage IV or unresectable stage III NSCLC not amenable to definitive radiotherapy and PD-L1 expression ≥50% were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive pembrolizumab (200 mg every 3 weeks, for up to 35 cycles) or pembrolizumab in combination with four cycles of induction chemotherapy, stratified according to the presence of brain metastases and histologic subtype. Patients with non-squamous histology received cisplatin or carboplatin (AUC 5) plus pemetrexed, followed by pembrolizumab-pemetrexed maintenance; patients with squamous histology received carboplatin (AUC 6) plus paclitaxel, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded central review according to RECIST v1.1. Key secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 321 patients underwent randomization, with 160 assigned to pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 161 to pembrolizumab monotherapy. At a median follow-up of 38.7 months, median PFS was significantly longer with combination therapy than with monotherapy (16.1 months [95% CI, 11.0-34.1] vs. 6.9 months [95% CI, 5.5-9.3]; hazard ratio (HR), 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.74; P<0.001). Median OS was 50.2 months versus 29.9 months, respectively (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.56-1.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 54% and 19% of patients, respectively; grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events occurred in 13% of patients in each group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with treatment-naïve advanced NSCLC and high PD-L1 expression, the addition of platinum-based chemotherapy to pembrolizumab significantly prolonged PFS compared with pembrolizumab monotherapy.

title: From Diagnosis to Destruction: The Rise of Radioligand Therapeutics as Oncology’s New Pillar
Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus chemotherapy in previously treated locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer: final overall survival analysis of the Phase III OptiTROP-Breast01
abstract: Background In the phase 3 OptiTROP-Breast01 trial, sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with previously treated advanced triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), with a statistically significant overall survival (OS) benefit observed at the prespecified interim OS analysis. Here we report the final OS analysis with extended follow-up. Patients and methods Overall, 263 patients with previously treated locally recurrent or metastatic TNBC were randomly assigned 1:1 to sac-TMT (n=130) or chemotherapy (n=133). OS was a key secondary endpoint. Results At a median follow-up of 29.4 months, median OS was 14.7 months (95% CI 12.1‒20.1) with sac-TMT and 9.9 months (95% CI 8.6‒11.8) with chemotherapy (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.45‒0.80); 30-month OS rates were 26.8% and 13.2%. The OS benefit observed at interim analysis was maintained at final analysis and generally consistent across all subgroups. Subsequent antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) therapy was received by 27.8% of patients in the chemotherapy group. After adjustment for subsequent ADC therapy using the rank-preserving structural failure time model, median OS was 14.7 months with sac-TMT and an estimated 9.4 months with chemotherapy (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.39‒0.73); censoring analysis yielded consistent results (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.43-0.82). The sac-TMT safety profile remained consistent with previous findings, with no new safety signals. The most common grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events were decreased neutrophil count, decreased white blood cell count and anemia. Exploratory patient-reported outcome analyses showed numerically longer median time to deterioration with sac-TMT than with chemotherapy across all five evaluated health-related quality-of-life domains, with the largest differences for fatigue and pain. Conclusions These final OS data after extended follow-up demonstrate a clinically meaningful and sustained OS benefit of sac-TMT versus chemotherapy and further reinforce its role as a treatment option for previously treated advanced TNBC. No new safety signals were identified.

title: Extended follow-up of tarlatamab in patients with small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy in the randomized phase III DeLLphi-304 study
abstract: BACKGROUND: In the DeLLphi-304 trial, at a median follow-up of <12 months, tarlatamab significantly improved overall survival (OS; P < 0.001), progression-free survival (PFS; P = 0.002), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and demonstrated a favorable safety profile versus chemotherapy. We report efficacy and safety outcomes after extended follow-up in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this phase III, open-label trial, patients with SCLC whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1 : 1) to receive either tarlatamab or chemotherapy (topotecan, lurbinectedin, or amrubicin) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was OS. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed PFS, objective response, disease control, duration of response per RECIST v1.1, PROs, and safety. RESULTS: As of data cut-off (18 February 2026), median OS was 13.6 and 8.4 months with tarlatamab and chemotherapy, respectively (median follow-up, 23.3 and 22.8 months). Median PFS was 4.2 and 3.2 months, respectively (median follow-up, 22.2 and 21.9 months). Kaplan-Meier estimated OS rates at 12 and 24 months were 55.9% and 30.3% with tarlatamab versus 39% and 14.9% with chemotherapy; corresponding PFS rates at 12 and 24 months were 20.6% and 14.2% versus 5.9% and 2.3%. Objective response rate was 35.4% with tarlatamab, including six confirmed complete responses versus 20.4% with chemotherapy; at data cut-off, ongoing responses were observed in 31.1% (28 of 90) versus 3.8% (2 of 52) of responders, respectively. Sustained disease control for ≥52 weeks was observed in 24.4% versus 4.3%. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) led to treatment discontinuation in 3.2% versus 6.6%; grade ≥3 events decreased over time, with no serious TRAEs with onset ≥12 months. Cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred early in treatment and were predominantly low grade. CONCLUSIONS: With extended follow-up, tarlatamab continues to demonstrate sustained and durable clinical benefit and a favorable long-term tolerability profile versus chemotherapy, in patients with SCLC after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, supporting its use as the standard of care in this setting.

title: Final analysis of the Neotorch study: perioperative toripalimab in combination with chemotherapy for patients with stage Ⅱ/Ⅲ resectable non-small-cell lung cancer
abstract: Background Interim analysis of the Neotorch study demonstrated significant benefit in event-free survival (EFS) and major pathological response (MPR) rate for perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable stage Ⅲ non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In this article, we report the overall final analysis results of the stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients in this study. Patients and methods Eligible patients with treatment-naïve resectable stage II or stage IIIA, IIIB (N2) NSCLC were randomly assigned to receive toripalimab or placebo plus chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment (three cycles), adjuvant treatment (one cycle), and toripalimab or placebo monotherapy as maintenance treatment (up to 13 cycles). The primary endpoints of this study were EFS assessed by investigators and MPR evaluated by blinded independent pathologic review in stage Ⅲ patients, as well as the overall outcome in stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ patients. Results A total of 501 patients in China were included in this randomized study (toripalimab arm: N = 250, placebo arm: N = 251). Baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the 2 arms. At the final analysis (median follow-up of 48.2 months), the investigator-assessed EFS was significantly improved in the toripalimab arm, with a stratified hazard ratio (HR) of 0.52 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.39-0.68, stratified P Conclusions Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated durable and significant benefits in EFS, MPR, and OS in patients with resectable stage Ⅱ and Ⅲ NSCLC, with a manageable safety profile. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT.

title: Efficacy and safety of risvutatug rezetecan versus gemcitabine plus docetaxel in relapsed/refractory advanced osteosarcoma: Primary results from the ARTEMIS-011 phase 3 trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) osteosarcoma have a poor prognosis and high unmet needs for effective therapies. Herein, we report primary results from ARTEMIS-011, the multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 trial of risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez), a B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate, in Chinese patients with R/R osteosarcoma after ≥2 prior lines of systemic treatment. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients (≥12 years) were randomized 2:1 to Ris-Rez 12.0 mg/kg or gemcitabine plus docetaxel (GD), every 3 weeks, stratified by age and lung metastasis. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and safety. RESULTS: At data cutoff (June 17, 2026), 80 patients were treated with Ris-Rez and 42 with GD; median follow-up was 7.1 months. Median age was 21 years (IQR, 17-34) with 31 (25%) adolescents (12 to <18 years). BICR-assessed PFS significantly improved with Ris-Rez compared with GD (median, 5.5 vs 1.4 months; HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.20-0.55; P<0.0001). OS data were immature, with a HR of 0.51 (95% CI, 0.21-1.23). With longer treatment duration with Ris-Rez than GD (median, 4.5 vs 1.5 months), adverse events (AEs) were reported in all patients. No treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) led to death. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs occurred in 93% of patients with Ris-Rez and 83% with GD, and serious TRAEs in 64% versus 29%, which were predominantly hematologic. TRAEs led to dose reductions in 71% versus 26% of patients with Ris-Rez versus GD, respectively, and permanent discontinuation was infrequent (3.8% vs 2.4%). CONCLUSIONS: In ARTEMIS-011, Ris-Rez demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS compared to GD, alongside a numerical trend toward improved OS and manageable safety profile with dose modifications and supportive care, offering a promising new treatment option for patients with R/R advanced osteosarcoma.

title: CheckMate 8HW: One Checkmate, Several Moves Left
Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study
abstract: BACKGROUND: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment. PATIENTS AND METHODS: TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence. RESULTS: 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001). CONCLUSION: Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.
